threads.body: This introduces an O(cluster_size) scan of all metadata nodes on every span start just to detect SNI. Since the result is effectively a session-level property, consider computing/caching an `hasSniEndPoint` flag once per wrapped session (or once per `CassandraRequest` at creation) and using that boolean here, to avoid per-request iteration overhead on large clusters.

replies.body:
Addressed in f9caea20f59e7e7ea799af0969a8272c4879a8e5.

Analysis: CassandraServerTarget already rejects SNI endpoints when the session is wrapped. The request stores that result for its lifetime. Reading the stored target directly removes the metadata scan and makes start-time emission use the same request predicate as end-time preservation. The SNI endpoint tests now model the production invariant by passing no configured target.

Upsides: Span start no longer scans cluster metadata, and start and end agree on whether the configured target was emitted.

Downsides: The getter relies on CassandraServerTarget construction to keep rejecting SNI sessions. No material runtime downside identified.

threads.body: The early-return condition here is broader than the start-time condition used in `CassandraSqlAttributesGetter#getServerTarget(...)` (which may return null even when `request.getServerTarget()` is non-null). In that mismatch case, `server.address`/`server.port` can end up unset because onStart doesn't emit them and onEnd returns early. Consider aligning the condition so onEnd only returns early when the configured target was actually emitted onStart (e.g., by storing a boolean on the request/session or by reusing the same predicate used by the getter).

threads.body: `new HashSet<>(programmaticContactPoints)` will throw if the instrumented builder's `programmaticContactPoints` field is null. If the driver initializes this field lazily (or uses null to represent 'unset'), this will fail at runtime. Suggest defensively handling null (e.g., treat it as an empty set) before copying.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: The supported DataStax 4.4 and Apache 4.18 drivers initialize `programmaticContactPoints` to a new `HashSet` in the `SessionBuilder` constructor. The Apache driver also resets it to a new `HashSet` when it clears contact points. The driver does not use null to represent an unset value.

Upsides: Keeping the direct copy matches the driver's non-null field invariant and avoids an unreachable fallback.

Downsides: A custom SessionBuilder subclass that breaks the driver's protected-field invariant would still skip wrapping under the advice's existing Throwable suppression.

threads.body: This change makes `CassandraSingletons` and `telemetry()` publicly accessible. If this is only needed as an implementation detail to support advice/helper wiring, consider keeping the singleton package-private and instead passing the `CassandraTelemetry` instance via constructor injection from within the same package (or by relocating the helper that needs it), to avoid expanding the public surface area of javaagent internals.

replies.body:
Addressed in 11b8380fea749e5bec6fe1aea298b984ef029404.

Analysis: Byte Buddy copies the advice body into SessionBuilder, so the transformed Datastax class directly accesses CassandraSingletons. Package-private visibility causes IllegalAccessError before the helper constructor runs. CassandraTelemetry is already passed into CompletionStageFunction through its constructor, but that does not remove the transformed class's access to the singleton. Public visibility is required for this javaagent helper boundary and does not create a supported application API.

Upsides: SessionBuilder can run the injected advice and wrap sessions without IllegalAccessError.

Downsides: The javaagent implementation class remains publicly accessible at the bytecode level, though it is not a supported API.

threads.body: PR description says that when multiple targets are present they 'use one comma-separated address without a port', but `group` is built from `asContactPoint()` strings (which include `:port` for each entry) while `port` is set to null. If the intent is 'no server.port attribute' (but ports may remain embedded in `server.address`), consider clarifying the PR description. If the intent is truly 'without a port' in the address string too, then `combine()` should emit only hosts (and potentially drop bracket/port formatting) for the multi-target case.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: Multiple targets keep each target's port inside the comma-separated `server.address` value. Only the separate `server.port` attribute is omitted. The pull request description now states this distinction.

Upsides: The description matches the implemented attribute values and removes the ambiguity.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: `ofAddresses` does not guard against invalid entries (e.g., null elements) and does not wrap its loop/build in the same `try/catch` used by the session-based overloads. However, `CassandraServerTargetTest.unsafeExplicitContactPointAddressesHaveNoTarget` passes a null `InetSocketAddress` and expects `null` rather than an exception. To match the omission rules ('unsafe or malformed values omit the stable target'), handle null/invalid addresses by recording an invalid endpoint or catching `RuntimeException` and returning `null`.

replies.body:
Addressed in 6e2db379251dc043f7618d7dcceb0355e87b1b15.

Analysis: The explicit-address overload let invalid entries throw before the target builder could omit the target. Catching RuntimeException around endpoint collection and target construction applies the same omission behavior as the session overloads.

Upsides: Unsafe or malformed explicit addresses now omit server.address instead of escaping into session construction.

Downsides: The overload does not expose the specific malformed endpoint that caused omission.

threads.body: Parsing string contact points via `lastIndexOf(':')` makes unbracketed IPv6 literals **without** an explicit port ambiguous and can be misinterpreted as `host + port` (e.g., `\"::1\"` becomes host `\"::\"` port `1`, and `\"2001:db8::1\"` becomes host `\"2001:db8::\"` port `1`). This conflicts with `CassandraServerTargetTest.invalidContactPoints()` which expects those values to drop the target, and it can also yield incorrect stable targets in production. Consider changing the string-format contract to require bracketed IPv6 (`[addr]:port`) for any IPv6 host in configured contact points, or add stricter validation to reject cases that look like bare IPv6 literals rather than `host:port` entries. (Mandatory to make behavior deterministic and aligned with the test expectations/omission rules.)

replies.body:
Addressed in 1836202b229d0b1d5d098ccc84371faaf32113fa.

Analysis: The last colon cannot distinguish an IPv6 address segment from a port. Requiring brackets whenever the parsed host contains a colon makes the configured contact point format unambiguous and keeps bare IPv6 literals from producing a false stable target.

Upsides: IPv6 contact points now produce a stable target only from the deterministic `[address]:port` form, and tests cover apparent-port edge cases.

Downsides: Previously accepted unbracketed IPv6 contact points with a port now omit the stable target.

threads.body: The expected stable `SERVER_ADDRESS` in this test includes `:9042` on each endpoint even though the PR description (and the new unit tests in `CassandraServerTargetTest`) specify that when **multiple endpoints all use the default port (9042)**, ports should be omitted from `server.address` and `server.port` should be omitted. This makes the expectation inconsistent and likely causes failures once the stable-target formatting is applied. Update `configuredTarget` to omit ports for the all-default-port multi-endpoint case (e.g., `ip,127.0.0.2`) or adjust the contact points so at least one uses a non-default port if you intend to assert the inline-port form.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: The first endpoint uses `cassandraPort`, which Testcontainers assigns as the mapped host port for container port 9042. The second endpoint explicitly uses 9042. These are mixed ports, so the target builder must inline both ports.

Upsides: Keeping the expectation preserves integration coverage for the mixed-port target format.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: This change makes `CassandraSingletons` and `telemetry()` public, which broadens the javaagent instrumentation's accessible surface area. Since the call sites shown (`SessionBuilderInstrumentation`) are in the same package, this visibility increase appears unnecessary for compilation and can encourage unintended external use. Prefer keeping the class/method package-private unless there is a concrete need for cross-package access.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: Byte Buddy makes the transformed Datastax `SessionBuilder` access `CassandraSingletons` from another package. A prior package-private version failed with `IllegalAccessError` before `CompletionStageFunction` could receive the telemetry instance. The class and accessor therefore need public bytecode visibility across the advice boundary.

Upsides: The injected session-builder advice can obtain telemetry and wrap completed sessions without a linkage error.

Downsides: The javaagent implementation class remains publicly accessible at the bytecode level, though it is not a supported application API.

[General] Cassandra contact-point order is not significant—the driver merges these values into a `HashSet`—so preserving configuration-list order makes equivalent configurations emit different `server.address` values and can even select a different first-five subset. This also contradicts the PR's promise to sort order-insignificant endpoints. Sort the complete target in this reconstruction path.

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:
- line 96
- line 173

replies.body: Fixed in [b8694d25f3](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/b8694d25f35749cdacd2d0688c7bb2bc86ec7057). All Cassandra target reconstruction paths now sort the complete rendered endpoint list before capping, including mixed configured and programmatic sources.

threads.body: [Documentation] The overload derives the target solely from this collection, but these instructions tell callers to pass only builder-method contact points and to use the other overload for configured points. For a session combining both sources, following this contract silently reports a partial target. Require this collection to contain the complete original list from every source, as the PR description states, or merge the session configuration in the implementation.

threads.body: [General] This strips brackets before `DbServerTargetBuilder` can validate their use, so a malformed value such as `[node.example.com]:9042` is accepted and emitted as `node.example.com` instead of dropping the complete target. Brackets are valid only for IPv6 literals; reject a bracketed host without a colon before removing the brackets so malformed configurations follow the PR's omission rule.

replies.body:
Addressed in 7ec3c533582f5a0785265470782b63a52404eec7.

Analysis: CassandraServerTarget removes brackets before passing the host to DbServerTargetBuilder. The builder therefore cannot tell that a DNS hostname was bracketed. Rejecting a bracketed host without a colon preserves valid IPv6 literals and drops malformed bracketed hostnames.

Upsides: Malformed bracketed hostnames now omit the complete server target, and the parameterized parser test covers this case.

Downsides: No material downside identified
